correctness.rationale: Each star edge contributes trace 2 and each triple contributes trace 3; after separate degree normalization the mixed positive-semidefinite Laplacian has trace n and one constant zero vector, hence lambda_2<=n/(n-1). Equality iff L=(nI-J)/(n-1), which comparing hub-leaf entries forces 1-alpha=2/n, and comparing leaf-pair entries forces every co-incidence count c_uv equal to the same positive integer mu. Under pair balance, 3|H|=mu*C(n-1,2), and both block eigenvalues are explicit: n[1-alpha]/[2(n-1)]+n alpha/(n-2) on n-2 leaf contrasts and n^2[1-alpha]/[2(n-1)] on hub-versus-leaf, with unique branch intersection alpha=(n-2)/n. The classical 7-block Fano plane covers 21 pairs once. Independently computed exact rational mixed 8x8 matrices for Fano and all triples at alpha=0,.2,.5,.75,1 and found equality; numerical eigenvalues gave gap 8/7 at alpha=.75 and 4/7 at alpha=0; proof all n remains analytic.

value.rationale: It gives an exact nontrivial optimizer and all equality designs for a natural higher-order synchronization model; sparse triple designs preserve every local linearized mode at a fraction of interaction count. Precise limitations to local identical-frequency relaxation and separately normalized coupling are stated.

final_claim: For mean-degree-normalized star pairwise layer plus nonempty simple leaf-only triples on n>=4 vertices, the Laplacian gap never exceeds n/(n-1), and equality holds exactly at alpha=(n-2)/n when the triple family is a positive 2-(n-1,3,mu) pair-balanced design. A Fano seven-triple system on n=8 has identical full normalized Laplacian to all 35 triples for every alpha, attaining 8/7 and twice pure-star gap.
